claim: Period drives architecture, wardrobe, props and signage together so no shot has to hand-tag its own century. Reach for it when the furniture of the world must stay consistent — showa and near_future dress the identical street into two unrelated films.
method: identical subject sentence and seed in every panel; only the option clause changes. panels marked control render the untouched subject, because SDXL cannot express absence.

panels.clause: ancient, stone columns, clay amphora, torch sconces
feudal japan, wooden architecture, paper lantern, tiled roof
victorian, gas lamp, brickwork, wrought iron
1920s, art deco, vintage automobile, telegraph pole
showa era, retro japan, wooden shopfront, old vending machine
modern, contemporary, glass and steel, present day
near future, sleek architecture, holographic sign, drone
far future, megastructure, chrome spires, alien architecture
post-apocalyptic, ruined city, rusted debris, overgrown wreckage
featureless architecture, no signage, plain stone

review.issue: timeless ends on "no signage", the same negation problem, and the option is otherwise carried entirely by "featureless architecture" and "plain stone".
review.fix: "plain stone architecture, unadorned walls, blank facades" — three positives, no negation.
